title: Marshal Catinat, coded despatch from the camp of 'Inglesheim', 15 Sept 1702 (Aarau, Zurlauben archive, Dup.ta Nr. 93, f. 238; Cryptoole XX1702-1)

documents.shelfmark: Aarau, Aargauer Kantonsbibliothek, Zurlauben family archive, leaf marked 'Dup.ta', 'Nr. 93', f. 238 (signature unknown)
documents.route: Camp under Strasbourg ('Ingleshem', probably Lingolsheim beside the HQ at Eckbolsheim) -> probably Beat Jakob II Zurlauben, Zug

transcription.source: Lichtenberger 1 May 2016 (Klausis Krypto Kolumne comment 1) with Norbert's corrections (comment 30); all 47 lines checked against the images 28 Oct 2026, two groups changed
transcription.notes: Doubtful groups (1.18.14, 1.22.7, 2.01.7, 2.10.9, 2.12.13 cut by the fold, 2.01.13, 2.19.13) listed in ciphertext.txt. Page 2 ends in clear 'Je suis avec plus de verite', continued on p. 3.

system.summary: Numeric nomenclator with figures 3-464, no word division, 43% of tokens below 100 (probably letters); system not established.
system.notes: IC 0.0086, matches Feuquieres 1691 petit chiffre (Norbert 2016), not the Grand Chiffre of 1691 (IC about 0.005). Repeats show homophones 10=17, 22=277, 101=350 (Thomas, Tomokiyo 2016).

prior_solution.where: Klausis Krypto Kolumne 2016 thread and Cryptoole XX1702-1: unsolved

conditions.human_role: Project-level: pasted the catalogue task text and asked for the attempt; no target-specific intervention.
tools: ordered_low.py (annealed block boundaries scored on a French bigram model)

solution.what: Downloaded the three page images and Bazeries-More-Letters.pdf from Klausis Krypto Kolumne; saved the comment thread text.
Read the 2016 thread (46 comments): Tomokiyo's catalogue, IC comparisons, repeats; no decipherment.
Rebuilt ciphertext.txt from Lichtenberger plus Norbert's 17 corrections; 591 tokens, matches Tomokiyo's count; page 1 lines 1-3 compared with the image.
186 distinct, 64 singletons, IC 0.0086, 252 tokens at or below 99.
Low numbers as single letters in alphabetical blocks: annealed 25 block boundaries on a French bigram model over runs of consecutive low numbers.
Same search on synthetic French enciphered by an ordered block scheme with the real run lengths: letter accuracy 35-40%; and on randomly relabelled numbers as null.
All 47 cipher lines compared with the page images: two groups corrected, seven flagged doubtful.
Applied the project's Pignerol petit chiffre 1690 key (167 groups; same IC and low-number share): covers 247/591 tokens, 4-gram score -3.70 inside the relabelled-null range -2.98 to -4.06.
Compared the number-range profile with Tomokiyo's 8B code of 4 Apr 1702: 8B never uses 1-21 (11% here) and has 24% of tokens above 400 (6% here).
Grid layout with column = initial letter (Tomokiyo Item 4/8B): residues of the high groups mod k=5..30 against a permutation null; no k significant.
Synthetic grid codes (k=10, 13, 18) at 591 tokens: the residue test misses them too, so the real result says nothing.
Homophone constraints from the two long repeats (10=17, 22=277, 101=350) and the five contexts of 41 269: consistent with Norbert's 'l'armee', not testable further without key material.
Resampling estimate: a deciphered sibling in the same code of about 200 tokens would give values for about 70% of this letter, about 1000 tokens for about 97%.

Aargau catalogue (blocked by a browser check), Vault II-III, Tomokiyo, BnF fr. 6204 key list: no sibling, clear copy or key; Vault places the camp at Eckbolsheim from 14 Sept, so 'Ingleshem' is probably Lingolsheim.

outcome.method_basis: Ciphertext-only attempt with a key-structure hypothesis; the controlled search recovers only 35-40% of letters even when the hypothesis is true, and the real decode is gibberish.
outcome.notes: Real data scored -2.35 per token against -2.42 to -2.60 for relabelled nulls, a gap as large as the control's, so ordered low numbers are possible but unproven. No key, no crib.
